html:
Pierre Belain d'Esnambuc was a Norman sea captain who founded the first lasting French colonies in the Caribbean. He settled part of St Kitts in 1625, sharing it with the English of Thomas Warner.

With backing from Cardinal Richelieu's Company of the American Islands, he landed on Martinique in 1635 and built a fort at Saint-Pierre. Settlers from France and St Kitts followed, and others took Guadeloupe the same year.

He died in 1636, and his nephew Jacques du Parquet took over Martinique. The colonists fought the Kalinago and drove them off the island. Martinique became a sugar colony worked by enslaved Africans under the Code noir.
